{"id":"COR-395","title":"RepoScopedToken bypasses cluster discovery (entire repo mirror) + remove dead resolveAuthHostToken","description":"## Context

Audit of all token-resolution paths (during <issue id="0116e107-8166-415a-a98c-169579ae79dd" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-389/wire-refresh-if-stale-into-control-plane-token-paths-tokenforresource">COR-389</issue> / PR #1377) confirmed data-API and control-plane calls are context-aware, and `git-remote-entire` (clone/push) resolves its cluster context via `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json`. **One git-cluster path does not follow that vision**, plus there's a dangling helper.

## 1\. `RepoScopedToken` bypasses cluster discovery (the real gap)

`auth.RepoScopedToken` (`cmd/entire/cli/auth/repo_token.go`), used by `entire repo mirror` create + probe (`repo_mirror.go:153`, `repo_mirror_probe.go:182` → `waitForMirrorClone`), mints a repo-scoped token for a **cluster** resource (`https://<clusterHost>/gh/<owner>/<repo>`) but:

* reads the bearer via `LookupCurrentToken()` → `NewContextStore().GetToken(api.AuthBaseURL())`, and
* exchanges it at a hard-coded `issuer := api.AuthBaseURL()`,
* **never consulting** `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` to learn which core the *target cluster* trusts.

This is the same multi-core bug <issue id="0116e107-8166-415a-a98c-169579ae79dd" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-389/wire-refresh-if-stale-into-control-plane-token-paths-tokenforresource">COR-389</issue> (control plane), the data-API slice (PR #1377), and `git-remote-entire` (cluster discovery) each fixed for their surface — `repo mirror` was missed. Single-core it works; multi-core it ships the active context's token to the **wrong core's STS** (e.g. active context on `eu.auth`, cluster fronted by `us.auth`) → exchange fails or, worse, authenticates the wrong identity.

**Fix shape:** resolve the cluster's context the way `git-remote-entire` does — `clusterdiscovery.ResolveContextForCluster(clusterHost)` → exchange *that* context's login JWT at *its* core for the repo audience. Likely route the mint through a per-context manager (`NewRefreshingResourceProvider` or a repo-scoped sibling) rather than the bare `sts.Client` + `LookupCurrentToken()` direct path. The function's existing comment documents going direct for wire-form parity with git-remote-entire — re-validate that constraint against the discovery-based approach.

Entangled with <issue id="610b06cf-81d9-46a9-bda0-6d10e932709e" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-393/sunset-entire-auth-base-url-discovery-only-auth-resolution-entire">COR-393</issue>: `RepoScopedToken` is also one of the `api.AuthBaseURL()` env-read sites slated for removal there. Sequence/coordinate accordingly (this card can land as part of <issue id="610b06cf-81d9-46a9-bda0-6d10e932709e" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-393/sunset-entire-auth-base-url-discovery-only-auth-resolution-entire">COR-393</issue> or just before it).

### Acceptance

* `entire repo mirror` (create + clone-wait probe) mints repo-scoped tokens against the **cluster-discovered** core, not `api.AuthBaseURL()`.
* Multi-core: active context on core A, mirror on a cluster fronted by core B → resolves B's eligible context (or errors with the login hint), never silently exchanges A's token at the wrong core.
* No regression to single-core mirror create/clone-wait or to `git-remote-entire`.

## 2\. Remove dead `resolveAuthHostToken`

`resolveAuthHostToken` (`cmd/entire/cli/auth.go:83`) is now referenced **only by tests** — `auth status` / `logout` moved to `resolveStatusTarget` (+ the refreshing resolver, PR #1377). It's also a `TokenForResource` caller, so it falls out naturally when <issue id="610b06cf-81d9-46a9-bda0-6d10e932709e" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-393/sunset-entire-auth-base-url-discovery-only-auth-resolution-entire">COR-393</issue> removes that primitive. Delete it (and its now-orphaned tests) unless a caller is reintroduced.

### Acceptance

* `resolveAuthHostToken` is gone (or has a real production caller again); no test-only production helper left dangling.

18	// the data plane's auth gate deliberately hides suspended mirrors behind
19	// invalid_target rather than disclosing their state (an enumeration guard;
20	// see entiredb's validateMirrorRepoExchange). Callers that already know the
21	// mirror exists (e.g. the create flow's clone probe) use this to render an
22	// actionable message instead of the raw OAuth error.
23	var ErrRepoTargetUnknown = errors.New("cluster has no servable mirror at this audience")
24	
25	// repoExchangeTransportForTest, when non-nil, is used as the sts.Client
26	// transport by RepoScopedToken instead of the default. Test-only seam so
27	// the wire form (audience / scope / client_id) can be asserted without a
28	// live core. Production leaves it nil.
29	var repoExchangeTransportForTest http.RoundTripper

31	// SetRepoExchangeTransportForTest installs rt as the transport used by
32	// RepoScopedToken and returns a cleanup function. Test-only.
33	func SetRepoExchangeTransportForTest(rt http.RoundTripper) func() {
34		prev := repoExchangeTransportForTest
35		repoExchangeTransportForTest = rt
36		return func() { repoExchangeTransportForTest = prev }
37	}

39	// RepoScopedToken exchanges the logged-in user's token for a short-lived,
40	// repo-scoped access token usable against a data-plane cluster's git
41	// endpoints (clone / fetch / info-refs).
42	//
43	// The data plane's git gate rejects the raw login bearer (HTTP 403): it
44	// only accepts a token whose RFC 8693 audience is <clusterBaseURL><repoSlug>
45	// and whose scope is "repo:<action>". This is the same exchange
46	// git-remote-entire performs internally for the entire:// transport — the
47	// CLI does it in-process when it needs to read the data plane directly
48	// (e.g. probing a mirror's clone readiness).
49	//
50	//   - clusterBaseURL is the data-plane cluster origin (scheme+host, e.g.
51	//     https://aws-us-east-2.entire.io); a trailing slash is trimmed.
52	//   - repoSlug is the full surface-prefixed path (e.g. /gh/octocat/hello
53	//     or /et/<project>/<repo>), joined to the cluster URL verbatim to form
54	//     the audience.
55	//   - action is "pull" for reads or "push" for writes.
56	//
57	// The exchange targets the same core endpoint and client identity the CLI
58	// logged in against (AuthBaseURL + the provider's STS path, client_id
59	// entire-cli), so a successful login implies a usable exchange. Errors
60	// surface verbatim from the STS endpoint (e.g. invalid_target when no
61	// mirror matches the slug+cluster).
62	//
63	// The subject token is the stored login access token read directly, rather
64	// than routed through the refresh-aware tokenmanager — so this path does NOT
65	// silently re-mint an expired login JWT, even though one is now refreshable.
66	// This is a known gap slated for removal: COR-395 reworks RepoScopedToken to
67	// go through cluster discovery + the per-context refreshing provider (and
68	// deletes the dead resolveAuthHostToken alongside it). Two reasons it stayed
69	// direct until then: (1) historically `entire login` stored only a bare access
70	// token, so there was nothing to refresh — no longer true now that login
71	// requests `offline_access` and persists a refresh token, which is exactly why

170	//
171	// Repo-scoped pull tokens are short-lived (minutes) while the default wait
172	// is 30m, so a single token can't cover the whole wait. The loop re-mints
173	// from the (long-lived) login token whenever a probe comes back 401,
174	// rather than minting once up front. Re-mints are floored at
175	// minReauthInterval so a flapping STS can't be amplified into a re-mint
176	// every probeInterval ticks.
177	func waitForMirrorClone(ctx context.Context, out io.Writer, clusterHost, owner, repo string, timeout time.Duration) error {
178		repoSlug := "/gh/" + owner + "/" + repo
179		checkURL := fmt.Sprintf("https://%s%s/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack", clusterHost, repoSlug)
180	
181		mintToken := func() (string, error) {
182			return auth.RepoScopedToken(ctx, clusterHost, repoSlug, "pull")
183		}
184		token, err := mintToken()
185		if err != nil {
186			return fmt.Errorf("authorize clone probe: %w", err)
187		}
188		lastMint := time.Now()
189	
190		if timeout > 0 {
191			var cancel context.CancelFunc
192			ctx, cancel = context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
193			defer cancel()
194		}
195	
196		ticker := time.NewTicker(probeInterval)
197		defer ticker.Stop()
198	
199		cloning := false
200		for {
201			ready, status := mirrorAdvertisesHead(ctx, probeClient, checkURL, token)
202			switch {
203			case ready:
204				if cloning {
205					fmt.Fprintln(out, " ready")
206				} else {
207					fmt.Fprintln(out, "  ready to use")
208				}
209				return nil
210			case status == http.StatusUnauthorized:
211				// The repo-scoped token expired mid-wait; mint a fresh one from
212				// the login token (no dot, since this is a token refresh, not
213				// clone progress). Skip the re-mint if we just refreshed —
214				// otherwise an STS hiccup that 401s every probe would mint on
215				// every probeInterval tick.
216				if since := time.Since(lastMint); since < minReauthInterval {
217					break
218				}
219				newToken, mintErr := mintToken()
220				if mintErr != nil {
221					if cloning {
222						fmt.Fprintln(out)
223					}
224					return fmt.Errorf("re-authorize clone probe: %w", mintErr)
225				}
226				token = newToken
227				lastMint = time.Now()
228			default:
229				if !cloning {
230					fmt.Fprint(out, "  cloning")
231					cloning = true
232				}
233				fmt.Fprint(out, ".")
234			}
235			select {
236			case <-ctx.Done():
237				fmt.Fprintln(out)
238				// User cancellation (Ctrl+C) should exit quietly, not print a
239				// "timed out…: context canceled" line. NewSilentError signals
240				// main.go to skip printing; a real deadline still reports.
241				if errors.Is(ctx.Err(), context.Canceled) {
242					return NewSilentError(ctx.Err())
243				}
244				return fmt.Errorf("timed out waiting for initial clone: %w", ctx.Err())
245			case <-ticker.C:
246			}
247		}
248	}

250	// mirrorAdvertisesHead fetches the smart-HTTP ref advertisement and reports
251	// whether HEAD resolves to a real commit, plus the HTTP status so the
252	// caller can distinguish an expired token (401, re-mint) from a
253	// still-cloning mirror (200 with no resolvable HEAD, or 404/503). status is
254	// 0 for transport/build/decode failures, treated as "not ready, keep
255	// waiting". Auth is the repo-scoped token as HTTP basic-auth password, the
256	// same shape git presents over the entire:// transport.
257	func mirrorAdvertisesHead(ctx context.Context, client *http.Client, checkURL, token string) (ready bool, status int) {
258		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, checkURL, nil)
259		if err != nil {
260			return false, 0
261		}
262		req.SetBasicAuth("entire-cli", token)
263		resp, err := client.Do(req)
264		if err != nil {
265			return false, 0
266		}
267		// Drain before close so the transport can return the connection to the
268		// idle pool and reuse the TLS session on the next tick. Go only recycles
269		// a conn whose body was read to EOF before Close, and the Decode error
270		// returns below leave the body partially read. Drain to EOF, uncapped:
271		// the maxProbeBytes cap on the read below bounds the Decode *allocation*,
272		// but draining to io.Discard is O(1) memory, and a LimitReader cap
273		// shorter than the body would stop before EOF and silently defeat reuse.
274		// The client Timeout still bounds how long the drain can run.
275		defer func() {
276			_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort drain to enable conn reuse; copy errors are irrelevant
277			_ = resp.Body.Close()
278		}()
279		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
280			return false, resp.StatusCode
281		}
282		// Cap the body to prevent unbounded reads; ogen's api/client.go does
283		// the same for JSON. Smart-HTTP wraps the advertisement in a "#
284		// service=..." pkt-line header + flush; AdvRefs.Decode expects to
285		// start at the first ref line, so strip the wrapper first.
286		body := io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxProbeBytes)
287		var sr packp.SmartReply
288		if err := sr.Decode(body); err != nil {
289			return false, 0
290		}
291		var adv packp.AdvRefs
292		if err := adv.Decode(body); err != nil {
293			return false, 0
294		}
295		if _, err := adv.ResolvedHead(); err != nil {
296			return false, http.StatusOK // reachable, clone still in progress
297		}
298		return true, http.StatusOK
299	}
